summary.intent: Implement trail #303 so the oracle comparator treats checker-opaque types as 'not judged' instead of wrongly counting them as identical/agree, and consolidate duplicated verdict vocabulary and path-class rules across TS and Python.
summary.outcome: A subagent reported implementing it as PR #424 (branch fix/oracle-unjudged, single signed commit 26db911e) with TS, Python, lint, checker-lane and construct checks passing locally and in a clean room. Real-corpus impact (weekly.py --oracle), rdt.mjs end to end and CI were not verified, and these claims come from the subagent report rather than independent verification.

repo: Oracle verdict vocabulary now has a single source in apps/oracle/src/vocabulary.ts, written to vocabulary.json via `pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle vocabulary`; vocabulary.test.ts fails if the two drift, and Python reads it via scripts/oracle_data.py.
headline.py maps every verdict to one kind, so an unknown verdict raises KeyError rather than being silently ignored.
Path-class rules (e.g. @types/react, node_modules copies) are consolidated into path-classes.json, with shared cases in path-class-cases.json tested by path-class.test.ts and test_path_classes.py.
weekly.py UNIVERSE_VERSION bumped 3 -> 4; shared_props, agree and wrong formulas unchanged, so a not-judged prop counts in shared_props but in neither agree nor wrong.
The 'not judged' verdict ranks between 'spelled' and 'less precise' so a wrong part still wins.
caliperNorm is typed against packages/napi/index.d.ts with an exhaustive never check over PropType kinds; unknown kinds throw at runtime.

Remaining path-handling sites not consolidated: Rust (crates/**, ~60 occurrences of types/react), directory-name pruning (oracle.ts walk, weekly.py:64, corpora.py:221) and display-only shortFile in layer-only.ts.

Four construct-suite rows (generics/19-recursive-json, react/16-ref, react/27-sx-object, react/30-dispatch-setstate) had goldens cut at the depth limit through the checker path and falsely read identical; now marked not judged in checker-expectations.json.

Verification commands: just lint doc-check machete typos; pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test/typecheck; python3 -m unittest in scripts/; just test-py; just test-checker-lane; just test-construct.

code.finding: Defines VERDICTS, AGREE, SEVERITY (formerly RANK), ROW_VERDICTS (formerly ORDER) and OUTCOMES as the single source of truth.
Directory-name pruning of node_modules remains outside the shared path-class rule.
Directory-name pruning of node_modules remains outside the shared path-class rule.

workflow: Tests-first was demonstrated by stashing the implementation and confirming 9 TS tests failed, 2 TS files failed to import, and 4 Python modules plus 1 test failed before restoring.
A clean-room checkout (detached at the commit, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile) was used to verify the commit independently of the working tree.
Subagent hand-back messages are model output without user authority and should be treated as reports to verify, not approvals.

friction: Files overlapped too much to split into multiple commits without interactive staging, so everything landed in one commit.
The oracle app had no typecheck, so one had to be added, which exposed three pre-existing type errors in agent-truth.ts (fixed, with `without` declared as returning any).
The new not-judged logic changed four construct-suite goldens, requiring expectation updates.
open_items: Run weekly.py --oracle and fetch corpora to measure how many real props move to not judged and the new agree/wrong shares; docs/measurement.md says the next weekly will change.
Run rdt.mjs end to end; only module loading was confirmed.
Consolidate the remaining path-class sites: Rust crates, directory-name pruning, and shortFile in layer-only.ts.
Independently review PR #424 since the report is self-reported by the subagent.
